subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Riding the Leopard, Summer Shirts, Easy Broth, and More

bullets.section: Song I’m listening to yet again
bullets.title: Ya Habibi Ta’ala - يا حبيبي تعالَ - Lynn Adib & Zeid Hamdan
bullets.note: Lynn’s vocals are otherworldly. One of the top comments says it all: _liquid gold_. This is a short clip, and you will play it more than once.

bullets.section: What I’m wearing in the heat
bullets.title: Quince’s Mesh-Stitch Button-Up Sweater Polo
bullets.note: I normally avoid pure cotton, as I find it itchy, but my lovely lady wants to reduce synthetics (polyester, nylon, etc.) in the house and on our bodies. She suggested I try some of the cotton shirts from Quince, and this polo ended up being a hit. It is incredibly breathable, nearly impossible for me to wrinkle, and uses Organic Content Standard (OCS) certified cotton fiber that isn’t treated with pesticides, insecticides, or herbicides.

bullets.section: What I’m drinking in the mornings
bullets.title: Brodo Bone Broth
bullets.note:
Broth is one of the easiest ways to get quality protein and nutrition first thing in the morning. For the past two months, I’ve been having 1–2 Brodo packets per day, often simply poured into a mug and microwaved for 60 seconds.  
​  
Brodo was founded by Chef Marco Canora, who was one of my primary teachers in [_The 4-Hour Chef_](https://www.amazon.com/4-Hour-Chef-Cooking-Learning-Anything/dp/1328519163/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20). ​Marco is the real deal. He won a James Beard Award for Best Chef: New York City, which is like winning an Oscar in the food world, and he has plenty of other awards and accolades to boot.  
​  
Brodo quickly became the most famous broth in NYC. The challenge for Marco has always been creating versions of his broths that (A) were shelf-stable, (B) met his high standards, and (C) didn’t require refrigeration… which he finally nailed.  
​  
My favorite flavors so far are Tuscan Sun and Tom Yum, which are included in [their sampler box](https://www.brodo.com/product/brodo-starter-box/). If you wanna get fancy, you can use a milk frother to buzz extra-virgin olive oil (I like [Kosterina](https://www.kosterina.com/collections/olive-oil?srsltid=AfmBOopBZkLLA1saWb-SVIxXPTXZ5SDJGImdjbmJx3vtSHAGygA9dvie)) into Tuscan Sun, and you can squeeze some lime juice into the Tom Yum for extra pop.
